rejectedSingle: it is the only {type} with these conditions ({conditions}), and a single frame would carry all its noise into the master, so it is not used

noDark.lightsWithoutExposure: the light frames do not declare the exposure in the header, and without the exposure StarLight cannot check whether a dark matches
noDark.otherSensor: no dark was captured with the same sensor and the same dimensions
noDark.otherExposure: no dark has an exposure of {exposure}
noDark.lightsWithoutGain: the light frames do not declare the gain, while the {exposure} darks do
noDark.otherGain: no {exposure} dark has a gain of {gain}
noDark.nearestWarmer: the closest {exposure} dark is at {temperature}, {difference} warmer than the light frames (the maximum allowed difference is {tolerance} °C)
noDark.nearestColder: the closest {exposure} dark is at {temperature}, {difference} colder than the light frames (the maximum allowed difference is {tolerance} °C)

noDarkNotice.one: {description} calibrated {combined}, without a dark: {reason}. A dark with a different exposure, gain or temperature would remove the wrong thermal signal, so it is not used. The thermal signal and the amplifier glow remain; stacking reduces hot pixels if the exposures were dithered. To remove them completely, capture darks with the same exposure, gain and temperature as the light frames.
